steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The ship takes damage from the very start of the action shown in the video, before it visibly hits anything. Nothing else about the ships or stations should change.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

steps.message:
I fixed the hull damage on manual takeoff from a surface station's pad. It builds cleanly. I haven't run the game, so I haven't checked the takeoff in play or seen the hull readout stay at 100%.

**What the recording shows:** the player's ship is docked on a surface-station pad and does a manual takeoff, rising at a fixed 2 m/s. Hull integrity drops from 100% to 99% as soon as the takeoff starts, before the ship has visibly hit anything.

**Why it happens:** on a manual launch, the station frees the bay immediately (`SpaceStation::LaunchShip`). The ship then becomes a normal flying body while it is still resting on the pad with zero velocity. On the first physics step, gravity pushes it slightly into the pad. The station treats that touch as a ship landing on a pad it has no clearance for (`SpaceStation::OnCollision`), which damages the ship. `Player::DoFixspeedTakeoff` already has a step meant to prevent this: it lifts the ship 1 cm and gives it a small upward velocity of 0.05 m/s. But that step sat inside `if (from && !from->IsGroundStation())`, so it only ran at orbital stations.

**The fix** (`src/Player.cpp`, `Player::DoFixspeedTakeoff`): the lift and upward velocity now apply when launching from any station. The orbital-only part is unchanged: following the station's rotation and adding its spin velocity. With the ship moving away from the pad, the physics code treats any contact as separating and skips the collision and damage. This doesn't depend on which pad the ship uses, so it covers every pad of the station. Docking, auto-launch and ship behaviour at orbital stations are unchanged.
